I feel that watching a video of a giraffe being decapitated would disturb me far more than human decapitation. Am I human?

I certainly think so. I mean, both are disturbing but I think I would likely respond the same way...and I've certainly heard other people express the same thought: finding animal cruelty more disturbing than human cruelty. I suppose the argument may rest in empathy. The animal seems less deserving of cruelty whereas we can contrive an argument that perhaps the human was somehow more deserving of the action.

This is it, I think. Kids and animals are innocent and (in the case of domestic animals) usually completely trusting and without comprehension of what's happening to them. Which I would guess is why there's less outrage when wild animals are killed. Even people who are against hunting will usually just greet photos of a dead deer with a kind of, 'That's disgusting. Who would do that to a beautiful animal?' kind of attitude (unless they're really extreme in their views), but if someone shoots a dog, people (even people in favour of hunting) will be ready to kill that person.

The uproar over horse slaughter is a great example of this. Lots of people are morally opposed to the slaughter and eating of horses, because horses are pets and our friends, but they really don't care one stitch about cattle, pigs or sheep.

Kids and pets love and trust people and won't understand why they're being hurt by them. Even though it's sad and upsetting when an adult human is killed, an adult can comprehend what's happening, etc.

I think you have never seen a video of a human being decapitated. I highly urge you to avoid it. It is way more disturbing than you think. I'll never forget seeing those guys beheaded back in the 90's in Iraq.

That said, seeing those Giraffe pics floating around lately, breaks my heart. Giraffes seem so nice with their long necks and long eyelashes.

Unfortunately I have seen a straight beheading of a human before. It was horrible, of course.

But it really didn't make a lasting impression on me. I am curious as to whether this is because I've been exposed to far more graphic and increasingly realistic violence in entertainment that it made it easier to accept the real imagery. And the lack of animal cruelty means that I just can't imagine it before I see it.

I have no intent of discovering which is more disturbing to me, as even talking about it now makes my stomach turn. The original submission was just a thought I had.
If you're talking about a beheading carried out by ISIL, that seems reasonable. If you're talking about one performed by the cartels, you might consider seeking treatment.

I'm sure both are disturbing to watch. Neither of which I want to watch anyway. Animals don't have a say in anything, there for I think garner more empathy, to me they are more innocent, more fragile than humans. I bet a vast majority would be more upset over the giraffe video, than the human video.
You will be more disgusted by what you are not used to.
